convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom for CMO indicator (non-built-in) and includes external TradeAlgorithms.mqh library for trade execution logic, requiring custom indicator replication and library function porting

derived_values.name: Time shift in seconds for signal timestamp

other_exits: Long position closed when CMO crosses below zero (Value[1]<0 and Value[0]>0 triggers BUY_Close)
Short position closed when CMO crosses above zero (Value[1]>0 and Value[0]<0 triggers SELL_Close)

position_sizing.conditional_logic: negative MM values treated as fixed lot size (e.g. -0.1 means 0.1 lots), positive values treated as deposit fraction for money management

custom_logic_notes: Signal uses two-bar CMO values: CMO[1] (previous bar) must be above/below zero, and CMO[0] (current bar) must be on opposite side. When SignalBar=0, signals are recalculated every tick instead of only on new bars. The BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/BuyPosClose/SellPosClose boolean inputs act as permission gates allowing independent control of entry and exit directions. TradeAlgorithms.mqh handles actual order placement with signal timestamp for potential re-entry prevention.
python_conversion_notes: The CMO indicator must be reimplemented in Python (Chande Momentum Oscillator: sum of up diffs / sum of absolute diffs * 100, then smoothed by Method). The TradeAlgorithms.mqh functions (BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, GlobalVariableDel_, LoadHistory, CIsNewBar) need Python equivalents. The conditional MM logic (negative=lot, positive=fraction) must be preserved. SL/TP are in points (not pips) so no digit adjustment is needed, but point-to-price conversion depends on symbol digits. The IsNewBar pattern with static CIsNewBar class translates to a bar-detection utility. The SignalBar parameter allows using bar[1] (completed) or bar[0] (forming) for signal reading.
